heroHeadline: Season Effectively Ends: CIFFC Drops National Preparedness to Level 2, Issues Final Situation Report of 2026
heroSubtitle: The Canadian Interagency Forest Fire Centre lowered the National Preparedness Level from 3 to 2 in its September 16 report — the last weekly national situation report of the season — citing no remaining priority fires and fire count/area burned nationally near or below the 10-year average. CIFFC will publish a full season summary later in the fall, with weekly reporting resuming in spring 2027. The Rinker Lake Complex in Northwestern Ontario (Thunder Bay 36, Dryden 34/35) remains formally not under control but with activity staying low, and BC's Bald Range, Pear Lake and Ainslie Creek fires all remain in 'under control' or 'being held' status. No new deaths, evacuation orders, or significant fire starts were identified this cycle.
footerNote: Data sourced from official reports, major outlets, and institutional analyses.
